title: Separate anatomical rig segmentation from dense Body sampling
description:
## User Mandate

> Sythesize these audits of the skeeltal mesh system and then help improve the bone vertex weights. The feet are also no longer flat on the ground, but that's a seperate issue, I think

STRICT. Keep the separate foot-grounding issue outside this rig-topology task.

## Summary
Introduce a compact anatomical rig segmentation layer so dense Body morphology samples no longer define the long-term character skeleton topology.

## Scope
- Preserve dense Body samples for morphology, SDF generation, and appearance.
- Derive a compact body rig with a pelvis/hip region, torso/spine segments, and applicable neck/head/tail regions.
- Select the pelvis/root region from stable limb attachment evidence, with a documented fallback only when anatomy is insufficient.
- Preserve semantic limb chains, mirror contracts, stable IDs, and the pure runtime/editor boundary.
- Define the future synthetic Root and local-space pose contract as a later decision, not an incidental hierarchy change.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Changing Body morphology sample density does not change compact rig topology or semantic bone IDs for the same authored anatomy.
- Valid generated creatures have a documented single anatomical root contract.
- Limb attachment and mirror behavior remain deterministic and source-verified.
- Weight authoring receives stable domain metadata suitable for the child weighting refinement task.
- Focused runtime tests and Unity validation cover representative biped and quadruped-like definitions.

## Validation
Run runtime builds and focused skeleton tests. Run Unity PlayMode or editor validation for representative generated creatures and record the exact result.

## Findings
Both supplied audits independently identify one-bone-per-Body-sample as an architectural coupling. This is an accepted P1 design follow-up, separate from the confirmed pose-rotation defect and the completed MVP weighting task.

## Blockers
The current world-space identity-host contract must be retained or deliberately replaced with a documented local-space pose contract. Do not add a cosmetic synthetic root.

## Next Step
Write the rig segmentation contract and compare compact topology against two Body sample densities before implementation.
